title: Pullback compatibility of the supported-Hom identification
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $h:X'\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and form the Cartesian square with $Z'=X'\times_XZ$, $i':Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ and $g:Z'\to Z$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $F$ be a bounded-below complex of etale $A$-module sheaves and let $a\in\mathbf Z$; use the ordinary module derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the inverse and direct images of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and supported cohomology of [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Write
$$
\chi_{i,F}^a:H_Z^a(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(i_*A_Z,F[a])
$$
for the canonical supported-Hom identification induced by [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]. Let $c:h^{-1}i_*A_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}i'_*A_{Z'}$ be the canonical closed-immersion exchange, with the canonical identification $g^{-1}A_Z=A_{Z'}$. Then for every $\alpha\in H_Z^a(X,F)$,
$$
\chi_{i',h^{-1}F}^a(h^*\alpha)=h^{-1}(\chi_{i,F}^a(\alpha))\circ c^{-1}.
$$
Here $h^*$ on supported groups is the canonical pullback in the localization sequence [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], and the right side uses exact inverse image and its canonical shift comparison. The same equality holds on the small pro-etale sites for $F_{\mathrm{proet}}=\nu_X^{-1}F$, with $\chi$ the identification of [lem-pur-supported-hom] and the canonical supported-constant comparison there; $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ is [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The two identifications agree under the site comparison: let $\nu^*:H^a_Z(X_{\mathrm{et}},F)\to H^a_Z(X_{\mathrm{proet}},F_{\mathrm{proet}})$ be the map induced by the exact inverse image $\nu_X^{-1}$ on derived supported sections, and $\gamma:\nu_X^{-1}i_*A_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*A_Z$ the canonical supported-constant comparison; then $\chi^{a,\mathrm{proet}}_{i,F_{\mathrm{proet}}}(\nu^*\alpha)=\nu_X^{-1}(\chi^a_{i,F}(\alpha))\circ\gamma^{-1}$, and likewise on $X'$. These comparisons commute with $h^*$ and with $c$, so the etale equality is carried to the pro-etale one. No finiteness hypothesis on $h$ or on $X'$ and no purity isomorphism is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-supported-constant-exchange-normalization] to the etale pullback, pro-etale pullback, and site comparison. It gives exact $L$, the actual canonical isomorphisms $d=c$ or $\gamma$, and $dL\rho=\rho'q$. Thus none of the maps below is an arbitrarily chosen exchange.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-supported-hom-cocycle-normalization], the module categories have enough injectives and $\theta_M(f)=(f\rho)(1)$ identifies supported sections with $\operatorname{Hom}(P,M)$, with the prescribed derived normalization $\chi$. The exchange identity of step 1 gives $d^{-1}\rho'=L\rho\,q^{-1}$. Since $q$ carries the pulled-back constant $1$ to $1$, evaluation gives $\theta'_{LM}(Lf\,d^{-1})=\lambda_M\theta_M(f)$. Restrictions to the open are zero on both sides. This verifies the underived hypothesis of the next step.

source.place: Section 9, Example 9.5 and Ext proof of Theorem 9.4, pp. 66–67; module-valued, bounded-below and pro-etale normalization made explicit in original item steps 4 and 6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-derived-representable-transport] with these $P,P',S=\Gamma_Z,S'=\Gamma_{Z'},\theta,\theta',L,d,\lambda$. Its normalized injective comparison computes canonical derived pullback and gives $\chi'(h^*\alpha)=L(\chi(\alpha))d^{-1}$ in every integer degree, including $L=\nu_X^{-1}$. The functorial localization pullback in [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] is this derived kernel map: the open and total-section maps inducing it are precisely the inverse-image section maps defining $\lambda$. Hence the three instances give the required etale, pro-etale and site-comparison equalities for the stated $F$.

proof.text: The underived constant-exchange square and supported-section square commute by [lem-pur-supported-constant-exchange-normalization]. Apply the composition and coherent-identification clause of [lem-pur-derived-representable-transport] to these squares. It identifies their derived pullbacks under $\nu_{X'}^{-1}h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\cong h_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}\nu_X^{-1}$ and makes the Hom formulas commute as well. Thus comparison carries the etale equality to the pro-etale one on both $X$ and $X'$. No finiteness or purity hypothesis has entered.
